extracted.intended_audience: users of the GAP computer algebra system (mathematicians / programmers writing GAP code)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference material describing semantics, representations, and functions for GAP lists, ranges, boolean lists, enumerators, and row vectors, including preconditions, effects, and examples for each operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: ListX
rubrics_metrics.description: ListX(arg1, arg2, ..., func) (function) — constructs a list by combining arguments according to a binary comparison operation and a pair function (example shows using < to produce ordered pairs satisfying a condition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: ListX(l,l, <, pair) produces [ [1,2], [1,3], [1,4], [2,3], [2,4], [3,4] ]. Use ListX to build lists of values computed from argument domains; SumX and ProductX use the same argument semantics to sum/product over the resulting list.

rubrics_metrics.name: SetX
rubrics_metrics.description: SetX(arg1, arg2, ..., func) (function) — like ListX but the result list of SetX is strictly sorted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Semantics identical to ListX except the result is sorted and treated as a set (no particular mention of duplicate removal beyond sorting).

rubrics_metrics.name: SumX
rubrics_metrics.description: SumX(arg1, arg2, ..., func) (function) — returns the sum of the elements in the list obtained by ListX when called with the same arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when you want to compute a sum over combinatorial combinations defined by ListX arguments; behaves as Sum of the ListX result.

rubrics_metrics.name: ProductX
rubrics_metrics.description: ProductX(arg1, arg2, ..., func) (function) — returns the product of the elements in the list obtained by ListX when called with the same arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous to SumX but multiplies elements instead of summing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Range (definition and syntax)
rubrics_metrics.description: A range is a dense list of integers in arithmetic progression (or degression). Syntax: [ first, second .. last ] or [ first .. last ] when increment is 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If first > last then [first..last] is the empty list. If second > first > last or second < first < last then [first, second .. last] is empty. If first = last it's a singleton. last-first must be divisible by (second-first) otherwise an error is signalled. Integers and length of a range must be small integers (chapter 14). A range is a special case of a list so list operations apply; assignment can convert a range to a plain list (representation rules explained).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsRange
rubrics_metrics.description: IsRange(obj) (Category) — tests if object obj is a range, i.e., a dense list of integers that is also a range (per the definition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: IsRange([1,2,3]) true; IsRange([1,2,4,5]) false; IsRange([]) true. Use to check the mathematical property (not internal representation).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsRangeRep
rubrics_metrics.description: IsRangeRep(obj) (Representation) — tests whether obj is represented internally as a range (storing only first, increment, last).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish from IsRange: lists created by syntactic construct [first, second .. last] are in IsRangeRep. If an IsRangeRep object is modified by assignment or Add/Append it may be converted to a plain list even if still mathematically a range.

rubrics_metrics.name: ConvertToRangeRep
rubrics_metrics.description: ConvertToRangeRep(list) (function) — if list is a range then change its representation to IsRangeRep; ignored for lists that are not ranges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to compactly represent a list known to be a range. Example shows converting [1,2,...,10] to [1..10].

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumerator (concept)
rubrics_metrics.description: An enumerator is an immutable list that can compute the i-th element and the position of a given object from basic data rather than storing all elements explicitly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerators can save memory and sometimes be faster than binary search in a sorted list; useful for huge domains (e.g., permutation groups). Use Enumerator and EnumeratorSorted functions to get enumerators; there are generic constructors like EnumeratorByFunctions and EnumeratorByBasis. For simple looping without enumerator facilities, use iterators (30.8).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsQuickPositionList
rubrics_metrics.description: IsQuickPositionList(list) (filter) — indicates that a position test in list is quicker than about 5 or 6 element comparisons for 'smaller'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If true, Position(list,...) may be efficient; can be beneficial to use Position and a bit list rather than ordered lists to represent subsets of list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain lists (concept)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plain lists are the default representation storing all entries explicitly; other representations include ranges, strings, blists, enumerator-based representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often representation doesn't matter, but when performance/representation-specific methods are installed it matters; PlainListCopy returns a plain-list representation copy for rare needs (e.g., before objectifying or calling kernel functions).

rubrics_metrics.name: PlainListCopy
rubrics_metrics.description: PlainListCopy(list) (function) — returns a list equal to its argument in a plain list representation (IsPlistRep).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended for rare situations where a plain-list rep is required before certain operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsPlistRep
rubrics_metrics.description: IsPlistRep(obj) (Representation) — returns true if obj is a plain list representation and false otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists entered as comma-separated values are usually plain lists. Examples: IsPlistRep([1,2,3]) true; IsPlistRep('abc') false; IsPlistRep([1..5]) false.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boolean list (IsBlist) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: IsBlist(obj) (Category) — a boolean list ('blist') is a list with no holes that contains only true and false.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boolean lists can have a compact internal representation (1 bit per entry). They are useful to describe subsets of finite sets where positions encode membership. Examples show IsBlist([]) true, IsBlist([false,,true]) false (# has holes), IsBlist([1,1,0,0]) false (# contains non-boolean values).

rubrics_metrics.name: BlistList
rubrics_metrics.description: BlistList(list, sub) (function) — returns a boolean list blist of same length as list such that blist[i] is true iff list[i] is in sub.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: list need not be a proper set and may contain duplicates; sub may contain elements not in list (they have no influence). Example: BlistList([1..10],[2,3,5,7]) gives boolean positions. See also UniteBlistList for a faster combined operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: ListBlist
rubrics_metrics.description: ListBlist(list, blist) (function) — returns the sublist of list represented by boolean list blist; blist must have same length as list and list must have no holes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: sub contains list[i] where blist[i] is true; order preserved. Example given.

rubrics_metrics.name: SizeBlist
rubrics_metrics.description: SizeBlist(blist) (function) — returns the number of entries in blist that are true (size of the represented subset).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: SizeBlist([false,true,false,true,false]) returns 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsSubsetBlist
rubrics_metrics.description: IsSubsetBlist(blist1, blist2) (function) — returns true if blist2 is a subset of blist1 (same length), false otherwise; blist2 is subset of blist1 if for all i, blist1[i] = blist1[i] or blist2[i].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check subset relation of boolean-lists representing subsets; example demonstrates true/false outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: UnionBlist
rubrics_metrics.description: UnionBlist(blist1, blist2[, ...]) or UnionBlist(list) (function) — nondestructive union of boolean lists of equal length; second form unions all blists in a list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns a new boolean list with position-wise OR of inputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: IntersectionBlist
rubrics_metrics.description: IntersectionBlist(blist1, blist2[, ...]) or IntersectionBlist(list) (function) — nondestructive intersection of boolean lists of equal length; second form intersects all blists in a list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns a new boolean list with position-wise AND of inputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: DifferenceBlist
rubrics_metrics.description: DifferenceBlist(blist1, blist2) (function) — returns the asymmetric set difference of two boolean lists of equal length: position-wise (blist1[i] and not blist2[i]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nondestructive counterpart of SubtractBlist; example given.

rubrics_metrics.name: UniteBlist
rubrics_metrics.description: UniteBlist(blist1, blist2) (function) — destructively unites blist1 with blist2 (same length), equivalent to assigning blist1[i] := blist1[i] or blist2[i] for all i; returns nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when in-place modification of blist1 is desired for performance. UnionBlist is the nondestructive counterpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: UniteBlistList
rubrics_metrics.description: UniteBlistList(list, blist, sub) (function) — works like UniteBlist(blist, BlistList(list, sub)) but avoids intermediate blist for better performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for efficient in-place union when converting a sublist to a blist and uniting it with existing blist.

rubrics_metrics.name: IntersectBlist
rubrics_metrics.description: IntersectBlist(blist1, blist2) (function) — destructively intersects blist1 with blist2 (same length), equivalent to assigning blist1[i] := blist1[i] and blist2[i] for all i; returns nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IntersectionBlist is the nondestructive counterpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: SubtractBlist
rubrics_metrics.description: SubtractBlist(blist1, blist2) (function) — destructively subtracts blist2 from blist1 (equal lengths), equivalent to assigning blist1[i] := blist1[i] and not blist2[i] for all i; returns nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DifferenceBlist is the nondestructive counterpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: MeetBlist
rubrics_metrics.description: MeetBlist(blist1, blist2) (function) — returns true if there exists a position at which both blist1 and blist2 contain true (equivalent but faster than SizeBlist(IntersectionBlist(...)) <> 0). Error if lengths differ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to test nonempty intersection quickly; example demonstrates behaviour and necessity of equal lengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: FlipBlist
rubrics_metrics.description: FlipBlist(blist) (function) — changes every entry true to false and vice versa; returns nothing (in-place).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FlipBlist(blist1) is equivalent to SubtractBlist(blist2, blist1); blist1 := blist2 when blist2 all true, but FlipBlist is faster and simpler. Examples show usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: SetAllBlist
rubrics_metrics.description: SetAllBlist(blist) (function) — changes every entry in blist to true (in-place); returns nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalent to UniteBlist(blist1, blist2) when blist2 all true but faster.

rubrics_metrics.name: ClearAllBlist
rubrics_metrics.description: ClearAllBlist(blist) (function) — changes every entry in blist to false (in-place); returns nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalent to IntersectBlist(blist1, blist2) when blist2 all false but faster.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boolean list compact representation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a special internal compact representation for boolean lists using 1 bit per entry; not every boolean list is stored in this representation and conversion rules apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dense lists read with only true/false are stored compactly. Results of BlistList, UnionBlist, IntersectionBlist, DifferenceBlist are represented compactly upon creation. If a function argument is in ordinary representation, it is tested and converted if it is a boolean list. Modifying a compactly-represented blist in-place so it remains a blist preserves compact rep. Converting a non-compact list to blist by changing it will not change its representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsBlistRep / ConvertToBlistRep
rubrics_metrics.description: IsBlistRep(obj) (Representation) returns true if obj is a boolean list in compact representation; ConvertToBlistRep(blist) converts blist to compact representation and returns true if possible, otherwise leaves it unchanged and returns false.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ConvertToBlistRep to attempt to compactify an existing list; examples illustrate behaviour when conversion succeeds/fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsRowVector
rubrics_metrics.description: IsRowVector(obj) (Category) — a row vector is a vector that is also a homogeneous list of odd additive nesting depth; typical examples are lists of integers/rationals/field elements/polynomials of the same ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matrices are not row vectors (even additive nesting depth). Additive operations must be compatible with list operations; not all row vectors admit multiplication via * unless entries are ring elements and category IsRingElementList holds. Methods for row vectors must require IsRowVector to ensure correct method dispatch. Example: IsRowVector([1,2,3]) true. Immutable row vectors are generally faster for algorithms that don't modify entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Row vector arithmetic semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions for arithmetic involving row vectors: vec1 + vec2 is pointwise sum when lengths and fields align; scalar + vec adds scalar to each entry; subtraction defined via additive inverse; scalar*vec multiplies scalar into each entry; vec1 * vec2 returns scalar (standard dot product) when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In more general situations mixing types/lengths can yield lists that are not proper row vectors or mixtures of types. Examples show mixed-type results. Mutability of results is governed by 12.6. Use matrix operations for further vector ops.

rubrics_metrics.name: NormedRowVector
rubrics_metrics.description: NormedRowVector(v) (attribute) — returns a scalar multiple w = c * v of v so that the first nonzero entry of w is an identity element (IsOne).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to normalise a vector so its leading coefficient is 1 (or IsOne). Example: NormedRowVector([5,2,3]) returns [1,2/5,3/5].

rubrics_metrics.name: Row vectors over finite fields / ConvertToVectorRep
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP can store row vectors over fields of order <=256 in compact representations for efficient arithmetic. ConvertToVectorRep(list[, field|fieldsize]) converts list to internal row vector representation (or rewrites compressed vector over given field).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forbidden to call unless list is plain list or row vector, field is a field, and all elements of list lie in field — violations can crash system. If list is already compressed and field omitted, nothing happens. Return value is field size used. Supplying field or fieldsize is faster and avoids mis-detection; compressed vectors have special display forms and behaviour for small lengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: ImmutableVector
rubrics_metrics.description: ImmutableVector(field, vector[, change]) (operation) — returns an immutable object equal to vector in the optimal representation for vectors over field; if change true the input may be modified to become immutable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If input is row vector, representation may change as a side effect but shouldn't be relied upon. Multiple calls with same field produce compatible immutable vectors for fast arithmetic without field conversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: NumberFFVector
rubrics_metrics.description: NumberFFVector(vec, sz) (operation) — returns an integer giving the position minus one of finite field row vector vec in the sorted list of all row vectors over the field with sz elements in same dimension; returns fail if vec cannot be represented over that field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for enumerator indexing and testing equality with enumerated vectors; example demonstrates mapping and comparison with EnumeratorSorted.

rubrics_metrics.name: AddVector / AddRowVector
rubrics_metrics.description: AddVector(dst, src[, mul[, from, to]]) / AddRowVector(dst, src[, mul[, from, to]]) (operation) — adds mul*src to dst in-place; if from/to given, only index range [from..to] is guaranteed affected; dst and src must be row vectors of same length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If mul omitted, adds src to dst. Changing dst in-place may be more efficient than allocating a new vector; three-argument form has no single-step operator equivalent.

rubrics_metrics.name: AddCoeffs
rubrics_metrics.description: AddCoeffs(list1[, poss1], list2[, poss2[, mul]]) (operation) — adds entries of list2{poss2} multiplied by mul to list1{poss1}; unbound entries in list1 are assumed zero; returns position of right-most non-zero element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If poss ranges omitted they span whole vectors; caller must ensure list2 has elements at poss2 and result will be a dense list. Function may remove trailing zeros. Example demonstrates result and mutation of list1.

rubrics_metrics.name: MultVector / MultVectorLeft
rubrics_metrics.description: MultVector(list1, mul) / MultVectorLeft(list1, mul) (operation) — calculates mul * list1 in-place; returns nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synonym behaviour: MultVector is same as MultVectorLeft.

rubrics_metrics.name: CoeffsMod
rubrics_metrics.description: CoeffsMod(list1[, len1], modulus) (operation) — returns coefficient list obtained by reducing entries in list1 modulo modulus and then shrinks list to remove trailing zeros; optional len1 restricts operation to first len1 elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to reduce coefficient lists modulo a modulus and clean trailing zeros; example provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: LeftShiftRowVector
rubrics_metrics.description: LeftShiftRowVector(list, shift) (operation) — changes list by assigning list[i] := list[i+shift] and removing the last shift entries of the result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performs left shift in-place, trimming the tail; used for polynomial/coefficient manipulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: RightShiftRowVector
rubrics_metrics.description: RightShiftRowVector(list, shift, fill) (operation) — changes list by assigning list[i+shift] := list[i] and filling the first shift entries with fill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performs right shift in-place, inserting fill values at front.

rubrics_metrics.name: ShrinkRowVector
rubrics_metrics.description: ShrinkRowVector(list) (operation) — removes trailing zeroes from list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to canonicalise coefficient lists; example shows [1,0,0] becomes [1].

rubrics_metrics.name: RemoveOuterCoeffs
rubrics_metrics.description: RemoveOuterCoeffs(list, coef) (operation) — removes coef at beginning and end of list and returns number of elements removed at the beginning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to trim outer coefficients equal to a given value; example demonstrates returned count and mutated list.

rubrics_metrics.name: WeightVecFFE
rubrics_metrics.description: WeightVecFFE(vec) (operation) — returns the weight of finite field vector vec, i.e., the number of nonzero entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic coding-theory weight function for vectors over finite fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: DistanceVecFFE
rubrics_metrics.description: DistanceVecFFE(vec1, vec2) (operation) — returns the distance between vec1 and vec2 (same length and elements in common field): number of positions where they differ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard Hamming distance for finite-field vectors; inputs must have same length and lie in common field.

rubrics_metrics.name: DistancesDistributionVecFFEsVecFFE
rubrics_metrics.description: DistancesDistributionVecFFEsVecFFE(vecs, vec) (operation) — returns the distances distribution of vec to vectors in list vecs; all vectors same length and field. Returns list d of length Length(vec)+1 where d[i] is number of vectors in vecs at distance i+1 to vec.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides histogram of distances; useful in coding-theory analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: DistancesDistributionMatFFEVecFFE
rubrics_metrics.description: DistancesDistributionMatFFEVecFFE(mat, F, vec) (operation) — returns distances distribution of vec to vectors in vector space generated by rows of mat over finite field F. Rows of mat must be linearly independent and lengths must match vec.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns list d as above counting vectors in the generated space by distance; used for code coset weight distributions and related computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: AClosestVectorCombinationsMatFFEVecFFE / Coords variant
rubrics_metrics.description: AClosestVectorCombinationsMatFFEVecFFE(mat, f, vec, cnt, stop) (operation) — searches f-linear combinations of rows of mat that use exactly cnt rows and returns a vector closest to vec; stops early if finds vector with distance <= stop. The Coords variant returns [closest_vector, v] where v is a length-2 list giving coordinates used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All vectors must have same length and lie in field f; rows of mat must be linearly independent. Use when searching for closest codeword with a given weight constraint; stop parameter allows early termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: CosetLeadersMatFFE
rubrics_metrics.description: CosetLeadersMatFFE(mat, f) (operation) — returns a list of representatives of minimal weight for the cosets of a code; mat must be a check matrix, code defined over field f, rows of mat linearly independent and all rows same length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computes coset leaders (minimal-weight representatives) for coding-theory applications; preconditions on mat and field must be satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vectors as coefficients (concept)
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of ring elements can be interpreted as a row vector or as the list of coefficients of a polynomial; GAP provides functions for arithmetic under these interpretations (lower-level support than full polynomial package).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functions in this section operate on homogeneous dense lists of ring elements; not all inputs may be empty; length parameters default to list lengths. Use these low-level ops for coefficient-oriented algorithms; see polynomials chapter for higher-level polynomial support.

rubrics_metrics.name: ValuePol (start of function)
rubrics_metrics.description: ValuePol(coeff, x) (operation) — given coeff as coefficient list of a univariate polynomial f and x a ring element, performs evaluation (function description begins here).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This chunk only begins the description; ValuePol evaluates a polynomial given coefficient list at element x (further details appear later in manual).
